subject: humanities
passage: The steel pan of Trinidad and Tobago was first made in the 1930s and 1940s from discarded oil ______ it is now played in concert halls around the world. Makers hammer the bottom of a barrel into a shallow bowl and then shape and tune separate areas of the surface so that each one rings with a different note.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "The steel pan … was first made in the 1930s and 1940s from discarded oil barrels" is a complete sentence, and "it is now played in concert halls around the world" is another. Two independent clauses can be joined by a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction such as "but," which also signals the contrast between the humble origin and the concert halls.
explanation.A: Correct. A comma followed by the coordinating conjunction "but" joins the two independent clauses.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon joins two independent clauses on its own; it is not used together with "but."
explanation.C: Incorrect. A comma alone can't join two independent clauses; this creates a comma splice.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "However" is an adverb, not a conjunction, so a comma plus "however" still joins two independent clauses with only a comma—a comma splice.
